note: Every colour in this file was measured with System.Drawing GetPixel on a real reference image. The source root, file, pixel coordinate and measurement method are recorded next to each value. Nothing here is quoted from memory. The rows flagged "measured": false are documented constants that have no lossless art source in this repository; their provenance is a URL, and they are kept separate on purpose. How many of each there are is in "counts" below, and tools/check-ui-data.ps1 recounts it rather than trusting it - an earlier draft of this sentence said "the four rows" when there were seventeen.
checked_by: tools/check-ui-data.ps1 - re-opens every source image and re-reads every recorded pixel. Run it after any reference drop. It is the only thing standing between this file and silent rot.

counts.note: Recounted from the entries by tools/check-ui-data.ps1 on every run, so these numbers cannot drift away from the rows the way the prose did. reproducible_by_pixel is every entry whose 'at' can simply be re-read; the one that is neither that nor a rect mean is text.java.container_title_crosscheck, which carries its own explanation.

warning: Two distinct visual languages are recorded here and they must NEVER be averaged or interchanged. java_container is the classic 1x beige/grey GUI with hard 1px bevels used by in-world screens. bedrock_screen is Ore UI, the flat dark out-of-world menu system. A colour from one language will look wrong in the other.
hex_format: #RRGGBBAA - alpha is always present and is never assumed to be FF
path_rule: An entry's repository-relative path is roots[source.root] + '/' + source.file, concatenated as plain strings. assets/ui/ui-screens.json carries the same map with the same keys and the same strings, and assets/ui/ui-atlas.json spells the same trees as referenceRoot + '/' + path; tools/check-ui-data.ps1 asserts the shared keys still agree.
join_key: atlas_id, where present, is the id of the sprite this colour was measured on in assets/ui/ui-atlas.json - the one join key between the three files. Entries measured on a Bedrock screenshot or on a 3x icon crop still name the 1x sprite they describe, and their own 'scale' field says by how much.

methods.histogram_mode: most frequent colour over the recorded rect; (x,y) is the first pixel of that colour
methods.run_scan: run-length collapse of a scan line; (x,y) is the first pixel of the run
methods.rect_mean: mean ARGB over a rect; use only where the source is lossy or dithered
methods.documented: not measured - taken from the cited URL

bedrock_scale_note: Ore UI screenshots are integer upscales of a 1x layout. The 3840x2160 Settings captures are 8x, the 835x420 dialog is 4x, the 2408x1080 Create-New-World capture is 2x. Divide a coordinate by the entry's scale to get UI pixels.

java_container.purpose: The classic container/window background. 40.5% of the 176x166 GUI rect and byte-identical across inventory, generic_54, furnace, anvil, beacon and villager.
2px inner highlight on the top and left edges, immediately inside the black border - the raised half of the panel bevel.
2px inner shadow on the bottom and right edges - the sunken half of the raised-panel bevel.
1px hard black outline around the whole panel, outside both bevels.
Fully transparent. Each corner is notched by a 2-3px triangle so the panel reads as rounded; 18 transparent pixels in total.
Outer 1px black border of the modern Java popup/dialog frame (nine-slice, border 6).
1px light rim just inside the popup border - the same grey as the classic panel fill, used here only as a highlight.
3px shadow band under the light rim, giving the popup frame its thickness.
1px black line between the frame and the dark well it encloses.
The dark interior well of a popup/dialog - much darker than a container panel.
Empty inventory slot interior. 40.2% of a rendered inventory screen - the single most common colour in the GUI after the panel grey.
1px slot shadow on the TOP and LEFT edges. Note this is the opposite side from the panel - that inversion is what makes a slot read as sunken.
1px slot highlight on the BOTTOM and RIGHT edges.
The top-right and bottom-left corner pixels take the FILL colour, not either bevel. Getting this wrong is the classic tell of a hand-drawn slot.
1px outline of a normal widget button (200x20, nine-slice border 3).
1px top and left highlight inside the button outline.
Button body. The sprite is dithered (22 distinct greys), so this is the modal colour over the body rect (3,3,194,14) at 41.1%, not a lucky single pixel.
1px bottom and right shadow inside the button outline.
Hovered/focused button: the outline flips from black to white. This is the whole focus affordance - nothing else changes shape.
Hovered top/left highlight - exactly +5 per channel on the normal state.
Hovered body - exactly +6 per channel on the normal body, with the identical dither pattern (same 41.1% modal share).
Hovered bottom/right shadow - +6 per channel on the normal state.
Disabled button keeps the black outline.
Disabled button is FLAT - no highlight, no shadow, no bevel at all. Losing the bevel is what communicates 'disabled', not a colour tint.

Amber hazard stripe on a destructive/warning button. The button underneath is the ordinary button (same #6F6F6F body, #AAAAAA and #565656 bevels, #000000 outline) with these diagonals painted over it.
1px outline of a slider track.
Slider track interior - the same near-black as a disabled button, and equally flat.
Focused slider track: outline flips to white, interior unchanged.
Slider handle outline (8x20 sprite).
Slider handle top/left highlight - identical to the button's.
Slider handle body. Dithered like the button; this single pixel sits in the #6C6C6C-#717171 cluster whose mode is #6F6F6F.
Slider handle bottom/right shadow.
Hovered slider handle body - +6 per channel, same rule as the button.
1px border of an unfocused text field - a single flat grey, no bevel.
Text field interior - solid black.
Focused text field border.
Scrollbar thumb body (6x32, nine-slice border 1). Note it is #C0C0C0, NOT the #C6C6C6 panel grey - close enough to assume and wrong if you do.
1px shadow on the scroller's right column and bottom row.
Scrollbar track - fully opaque black, not a tinted overlay.
Unselected tab body - black at alpha 219, a translucent overlay rather than a fill.
Tab left/right/bottom edge - black at alpha 191, slightly more transparent than the body.
The faint 1px white hairline inside an unselected tab, alpha 51.
Hovered tab: the same hairline goes to full opacity. Alpha, not colour, is the hover state.
Selected tab body is fully transparent - the tab opens into the panel behind it. Only the top edge is drawn.
Selected tab top edge, alpha 191, with a #FFFFFF alpha-51 hairline directly under it at (4,1).
Tooltip interior: a very dark purple-black at alpha 240, uniform across the whole 100x100 nine-slice. Never solid black.
Top of the famous two-colour tooltip border gradient - a bright violet at alpha 80.
Midpoint of the tooltip border gradient, measured on the left column at y=50.
Bottom of the tooltip border gradient - the same hue at roughly half the value. Alpha stays 80 for the whole ramp.
1px opaque black outline around the whole hotbar (182x22).
Hotbar top-left inner highlight.
Hotbar cell interior - a dark olive at alpha 186, NOT neutral grey and NOT opaque. Two mistakes in one pixel if you guess it.
The line between hotbar cells, alpha 186 to match the cell.
Outermost pixel of the selected-slot frame (24x23).
Soft alpha-174 dark band just inside the selection outline.
Top-left white corner of the selection frame.
Selection frame body, light band - very slightly green, not neutral.
Selection frame body, mid band.
Selection frame body, dark band on the inner edge.
The selection frame's interior is fully transparent - it is a ring, not a fill.

states.purpose: The mouse-over slot wash drawn BEHIND the item: white at alpha 96, filling the inner 16x16 of a 24x24 sprite. This is the number people always guess wrong.
The second, fainter mouse-over wash drawn IN FRONT of the item: white at alpha 32. Two layers, two alphas.
A disabled (crafter) slot: the bevel is INVERTED so the cell reads as raised and dead. Fill goes to the panel grey.
Disabled slot highlight on TOP and LEFT - the mirror of the normal slot.
Disabled slot shadow on BOTTOM and RIGHT - and it is the normal slot's fill colour reused as a shadow.
Disabled slot off-diagonal corners - a midpoint grey, unlike the normal slot which reuses its fill.

The dark L of a crafter GRID cell - the one place in 26.2 where the slot bevel is not #373737. Everything else about the cell is standard: #FFFFFF light L, #8B8B8B fill, #8B8B8B at both far corners. A detector that matches the dark bevel on an exact colour finds these nine cells missing and no others.

Top and left of the raised plate baked inside every crafter grid cell - a second, INVERTED bevel filling the 16x16 item area, light on the top-left where a slot is dark. Not the cell bevel, and not sprites/container/crafter/disabled_slot.png, which is a different overlay drawn at runtime.
Bottom and right of that same raised plate. Identical in value to the hovered slider handle body, which is a coincidence of the GUI's one-face-scaled-two-ways palette, not a shared element.
Outer frame of a craftable recipe cell (24x24 with a 1px black drop on the right and bottom).
Craftable cell inner shadow, top and left - same value as an ordinary slot shadow.
Craftable cell interior - identical to an ordinary slot.
Craftable cell inner highlight, bottom and right.
1px black drop shadow on the far right column and bottom row of the recipe cell.
THE RED STATE, measured losslessly. Outer frame of an uncraftable recipe cell. Note the bevel structure is byte-for-byte the craftable cell with every grey swapped for a red of the same value.
Uncraftable cell inner shadow, top and left.
Uncraftable cell interior - a DESATURATED grey, darker than the normal #8B8B8B. The red lives only in the frame and bevels.
Uncraftable cell inner highlight, bottom and right.
1px black drop on the far right column and bottom row.
Unselected recipe-book category tab body.
Recipe-book tab highlight.
Recipe-book tab shadow.
Selected recipe-book tab body - the tab lightens to the PANEL grey, so it merges with the page it opens.
The 'show only craftable' toggle when on - Java's one green accent in the container language.
Bedrock's classic-inventory empty slot: 71.4% of a clean 54x54 3x extraction, and IDENTICAL to Java's #8B8B8B. The two editions share the classic slot palette exactly.
Bedrock empty-slot top/left shadow - identical to Java's.
Bedrock empty-slot bottom/right highlight. Reads #FEFEFE rather than #FFFFFF because the 3x extraction is one step lossy; treat Java's #FFFFFF as canonical.
Approximate top/left band of the red 'uncraftable' slot. SOURCE IS LOSSY (AVIF-derived: 2000+ distinct colours in ~3000 px) - use java.recipe.uncraftable.* instead wherever possible.
Approximate interior of the red slot, taken as a rect mean over an 8x2 patch of a cleaner screenshot rather than a single lossy pixel.
Approximate light bevel of the red slot, rect mean over a 4x2 patch.
Approximate dark bevel of the red slot. LOSSY.
Bedrock classic-style scrollbar thumb - lighter than the #C6C6C6 panel it sits on.
Bedrock classic scrollbar groove - the same shadow value as a slot.

bedrock_screen.purpose: The near-white top header bar of every Ore UI screen. 7.9% of a whole 3840x2160 Settings capture.
1px lighter lip along the bottom of the header bar.
2px opaque drop shadow under the header bar. It is a solid colour, not a translucent gradient.
Header title text - near-black on the light bar, and the same value as the universal Ore UI border.
The main content-pane background - 56.7% of a whole Settings capture, so this is THE Ore UI page colour.
The darker left navigation panel - 24.3% of the same capture. Content is LIGHTER than nav, which is the opposite of most desktop UI.
Control: the same content background measured over four widely separated points of a screenshot with a live world behind it, all identical - Ore UI panels are OPAQUE, not translucent.
The single near-black border used by every raised Ore UI control - buttons, toggles, sliders, tabs, text fields. One border colour for the whole system.
Upper half of a content-pane groove separator.
Lower half of a content-pane groove separator - dark ABOVE light, which is what makes it read as a groove rather than a line.
Upper half of a nav-panel groove separator.
Lower half of a nav-panel groove separator.
Selected nav row - it lightens to exactly the content-pane colour, so the selection visually connects to the page.
Secondary/default button: 1px top and left highlight.
Secondary/default button body.
Secondary button: 1px bottom and right bevel - LIGHTER than the fill, not darker. Ore UI lights all four inner edges.
Secondary button: a 2px dark base lip between the bevel and the bottom border. This lip is the whole 3D trick of Ore UI.
Primary/confirm button: 1px top and left highlight.
THE Ore UI accent green. Confirmed on two independent 8x captures (Play screen and Settings/Video slider fill).

The same accent green as it reads on the 2x Create-New-World capture (100% of a 100x30 rect). Recorded rather than averaged: the difference is one unit of blue and it is a capture artefact. Prefer #3C8527.
Primary button: 1px bottom and right bevel.
Primary button: 2px dark green base lip.
Destructive button: 1px top and left highlight.
Destructive button body.
Destructive button: 1px bottom and right bevel.
Destructive button: 2px dark red base lip.
Realms button: 1px top highlight.
Realms button body - 100% of a 100x30 rect.
Realms button: dark purple base lip.
Toggle body when ON - the accent green, no separate 'on' colour.
Toggle ON: 1px light green bevel.
Toggle body when OFF - a mid grey, NOT the dark page colour. Measured on the same screen as an ON toggle so the two are directly comparable.
Toggle OFF: 1px light bevel.
Toggle knob body - the same grey as a secondary button, and it does not change between ON and OFF.
Toggle knob: 1px light bevel on the leading edge.
Toggle knob: 1px bevel on the trailing edge.
Slider track to the left of the knob - accent green.
Slider filled portion: 1px light green bevel.
Slider track to the right of the knob - a mid grey, distinct from the toggle-off grey.
Slider knob body.
SELECTED tab body - the DARKER of the two, matching the nav colour. Ore UI selects by recessing, not by lighting up.
Selected tab: 1px top bevel.
Selected tab: 1px bottom bevel.
UNSELECTED tab body - the lighter of the two.
Unselected tab: 1px top bevel - brighter than the selected tab's, reinforcing 'raised'.
Unselected tab: 1px bottom bevel.
Keyboard/gamepad focus is a 1px pure-white underline drawn INSIDE the control, just above its bottom border. There is no coloured focus ring anywhere in Ore UI.
Scrollbar thumb over the nav panel - the same near-white as the header bar.
Scrollbar thumb over the content pane - very slightly brighter than the nav one.
Scrollbar track - the same value as the secondary button's base lip.
1px pure black outline beside the scrollbar - the ONE place Ore UI uses #000000 instead of #1E1E1F.
Text field interior - the nav-panel darkness, recessed against the lighter content pane.
Text field border. Note it reads #1E1E1E on this 2x capture against #1E1E1F elsewhere - a one-unit capture artefact, not a second colour.
A settings/world list row card - the content-pane colour again. Rows are separated by grooves, not by alternating fills.
Modal dialog title bar and footer.
1px light lip along the top of a dialog header.
Modal dialog body - DARKER than its own header, the reverse of the main screen where content is lighter than nav.
Hardcore/warning badge chip - a pale red with #1E1E1F text on it.
LAN/informational badge chip.
Friend/positive badge chip - a pale green, NOT the #3C8527 accent.
Experimental/caution badge chip.
Neutral badge chip (game mode) - dark, with WHITE text, where every coloured chip has near-black text.

text.purpose: The container/window label ('Crafting', 'Chest'), drawn WITHOUT a shadow. Measured off a 1x render: only two colours exist in that rect, this and the #C6C6C6 panel, so it is exact.
text.note: The widely-quoted Java constant is 0x404040. What is actually on the pixels here is #3F3F3F. Recorded as measured; do not silently substitute 0x404040.

text.purpose: Independent cross-check of the container label on a lossy Bedrock screenshot - consistent with #3F3F3F once compression is allowed for. Do NOT use this value; it is evidence, not a colour.
text.reproducibility_note: NOT REPRODUCIBLE as recorded, found 2026-08-17 while writing tools/check-ui-data.ps1. GetPixel at the recorded (896,144) is #C5C5C5FF - a background pixel in the gap between two glyphs - and no rect anchored there up to 80x40, nor any rect up to 16x12 anywhere in the 90x60 window around it, has a mean of #4A4A4A. The title text really is on that row (dark runs at x 889..891 and x 907..912 measure #4C4C4C, #494949, #505050, #4D4D4D), and the mean of the dark pixels of the whole label comes out #4C4C4C, so the recorded value is the right kind of number and is consistent with the entry's own claim. The rect it came from was not written down and could not be recovered, so the value is kept unchanged and flagged instead of being quietly re-measured into something different. The checker counts it as declared-unreproducible rather than as a pass or a failure.

text.purpose: Ore UI body/heading text on a dark panel - 46.8% of a heading rect.
Ore UI subtitle/description text - and it is exactly the secondary button fill, reused as a text colour.
Ore UI text on any light surface (header bar, coloured chips, light buttons) - the same near-black as the universal border.

NOT MEASURED. The Java text shadow rule: shadow = (rgb >> 2) per channel, drawn at +1x +1y. #FFFFFF body text therefore casts a #3F3F3F shadow. Verified against the cited table's own foreground/background columns (255->63, 170->42, 85->21) for all sixteen codes.
Formatting code 0 (black). NOT MEASURED - no lossless art source for the font palette exists in this repository.

Formatting code 7 (gray), Java value. Bedrock uses #C6C6C6 for the same code. NOT MEASURED - but note #AAAAAA is exactly the measured java.button.bevel_light and #C6C6C6 is exactly the measured java.panel.fill, so the documented palette and the art agree.
Formatting code 8 (dark_gray). NOT MEASURED - but identical to the measured java.panel.bevel_dark.
Formatting code f (white) - the default body text colour. NOT MEASURED.
